faqs.question: What mesh sizes can you supply for dehydrated onions?
faqs.answer: While our standard grade is a fine 80-100 mesh powder, we can customize the milling from 40 mesh coarse powder up to fine flour. We also supply dehydrated onion kibbled, flakes, and minced grades.

faqs.question: How do you prevent onion powder from caking during maritime transport?
faqs.answer: We pack the powder in multi-wall kraft paper bags with heavy-duty PE liners (300+ gauge). Additionally, we place silica gel packets throughout the shipping container and utilize container desiccants to absorb ambient humidity in transit.

faqs.question: Do you offer steam-sterilized (micro-reduced) onion powder?
faqs.answer: Yes, we can provide steam-treated or micro-reduced onion powder on request. This process significantly lowers the microbiological load (TPC < 5,000 CFU/g) to meet the strict quality standards of infant food and ready-to-eat seasoning manufacturers.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Nutraceutical and Food-Grade psyllium?
faqs.answer: Nutraceutical-grade psyllium husk is held to the highest purity standards (typically 99%) and strict microbiological limits (TPC ≤ 10,000 CFU/g) for capsules and dietary supplements. Food-grade psyllium ranges from 85% to 98% purity, optimized as a functional binder, stabilizer, or texturizer in gluten-free baking and processed meats.

faqs.question: How do you test and measure the swelling index of psyllium husk?
faqs.answer: We test the swelling index using standard pharmacopoeia methods: 1 gram of psyllium husk is placed in a 100ml graduated cylinder filled with water, shaken vigorously, and left to stand for 24 hours. The resulting mucilage volume is measured in milliliters per gram. Our nutraceutical grades guarantee a swelling index of ≥ 40 ml/g.

faqs.question: What mesh size options do you offer for psyllium powder?
faqs.answer: We offer whole husk (30-40 mesh) as well as milled psyllium powder in 40 mesh, 60 mesh, 70 mesh, and fine 100 mesh sizes, depending on the requirement of your formulation.
